title: Causal runbook regression tester and auto-annotator
author: Aisha Kapoor
release_notes: Add a deterministic runbook regression harness and annotator for validating playbook steps against representative traces; integrates into CI as a gated job. No user-facing breaking changes.
description:
Title: Causal runbook regression tester and auto-annotator

Summary: This PR introduces a lightweight, deterministic regression testing harness for runbooks (slo-toolkit/regression) that replays representative telemetry traces, applies controlled causal perturbations, and verifies that runbook remediation steps map to the expected state transitions. It also adds an auto-annotator that enriches runbook steps with confidence scores, likely subsystem tags, and remediation heuristics derived from past incident traces. Goal is to detect regressions in runbook effectiveness and reduce manual review overhead when playbooks are updated.

Why: We've observed subtle regressions where runbook edits (text or commands) stop being effective against live-like telemetry patterns. Manual testing is slow and brittle. A reproducible harness that can be run locally and in CI will catch regressions early and produce actionable annotations to help authors improve steps.

What changed (high level): - New regression harness package: slo_toolkit/regression/causal_runner.py (deterministic replay engine, seeding, perturbation API) - A set of canonical trace fixtures in examples/trace-fixtures/ (kafka-lag, db-conn-spike, cache-thrash) - Auto-annotator module: slo_toolkit/annotations/auto_annotator.py (step scoring, subsystem classification, remediation hints) - CLI entrypoint: bin/slo-regtest (local run, matrix options, --seed, --replay-window) - CI: .github/workflows/runbook-regression.yml added (matrix over traces + python versions) - Docs: docs/runbooks/regression-testing.md (how to write testable runbook steps, acceptance criteria) - Tests: tests/regression/* (unit tests for runner, end-to-end smoke test)

Checklist: - [x] Add deterministic replay engine with seed control - [x] Provide representative trace fixtures and tooling to pare traces to shorter windows - [x] Integrate harness into CI as gated job (non-blocking for now, will gate next quarter) - [x] Unit and e2e tests for core functionality - [x] Documentation for authors and SREs

Commits (summary): - Initial harness scaffold and data model for trace fragments - Implement deterministic causal replayer with perturbation hooks - Add fixture traces and canonical examples - Implement auto-annotator and confidence heuristics - Add CLI and CI workflow - Address review comments: deterministic seeding, sampling size control, improved logging

Files changed (high level list): - slo_toolkit/regression/causal_runner.py - slo_toolkit/regression/runner_cli.py - slo_toolkit/annotations/auto_annotator.py - examples/trace-fixtures/kafka_lag.json, db_conn_spike.json, cache_thrash.json - tests/regression/test_runner.py, test_annotator.py - docs/runbooks/regression-testing.md - .github/workflows/runbook-regression.yml - bin/slo-regtest (executable)

Small illustrative snippets included in the diff: - deterministic seed usage: runner = CausalRunner(seed=seed, perturbations=perturbations) - annotator output example (CSV/JSON): [{"step_id":"restart-cache","confidence":0.82,"subsystem":"cache","remediation_hint":"increase-ttl-or-restart"}]

Review thread (high level): - Daniel Park (review): "Nicely scoped. Two concerns: 1) sampling may hide flaky failures — we should add a 'stress' mode that increases perturbation intensity; 2) logs need correlation ids so CI artifacts map back to traces." - Aisha (author): "Added --stress and --seed params and included correlation id header in runner logs. Also added sample_size control to CLI and documented mapping to CI artifacts." - Sofia Martinez (review): "Annotator heuristics look useful, but can we avoid leaking internal service names? Suggest mapping to public-facing subsystem tags and adding a redact option." - Aisha: "Added mapping layer and --redact option; updated docs to show anonymized outputs for public artifacts." - Liam O'Connor (approval): "Nothing blocking from SRE side; CI passed locally for matrix runs."

CI summary: - New workflow runbook-regression.yml executes matrix: traces=[kafka_lag,db_conn_spike,cache_thrash], python=[3.10,3.11] - Steps: install deps, run unit tests, run e2e smoke using --seed=42, upload artifacts (replay logs, annotator-json) - Initial CI run failed (timeout on long DB fixture), author trimmed replay window and added --max-duration flag - Final CI run: all checks pass; artifacts uploaded to PR (replay-logs.zip, annotator-results.json)

Backward compatibility and safety: - No changes to runtime behavior of on-call tooling; all new modules are opt-in via CLI and CI job - Annotator outputs include redact option and default to anonymized subsystem tags in CI uploads to avoid leaking internal mappings

Next steps (follow-ups tracked in Linear): - Gate the CI job in next milestone once we have 50+ runbook fixtures and a maintenance policy (ENG-2041) - Add a dashboard in Console to surface annotator confidence trends per runbook - Expand fixture corpus with customer-derived traces and privacy-preserving sampling

Merge: Squash merged to main after approvals and successful CI run.
